slides.say: Twenty-seven identical cubes, each with edge four, form a big cube. One corner cube is removed. How do the volume and the total surface area of the solid change?
We call these Rubik's cube questions, and the idea comes back quite a lot on the exam. We'll solve it by understanding, one part at a time.
First the volume. We take one cube out, so the volume goes down. One small cube is four times four times four, sixty-four. So the volume goes down by sixty-four.
at: So the volume goes down by

slides.say: Choice number one says the volume doesn't change, so it's out. The other three choices all say it goes down by sixty-four.
Now the surface area. This part is harder to see. What does the corner cube give to the surface? Three faces, the top, the front and the side.
Each face is four times four, sixteen. So if we take the cube away, it looks like we lose three faces, forty-eight. That's choice number three, and it's a trap.
at: Each face is four times four

slides.say: Why a trap? Once the corner cube is gone, we can see three faces that it was hiding. These are faces of its neighbors.
at: Once the corner cube is gone

slides.say: So we lost three faces, and we gained three faces. The surface area doesn't change. Choice number two is our answer.
at: Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: Careful, this is not a rule for every cube we remove. It depends on where the cube is. In Rubik's cube questions, there are three places to tell apart.
A corner, like in our question. It shows three faces, and three new faces appear. Minus three, plus three, no change.
at: A corner, like in our question

slides.say: The middle of an edge. It shows two faces. Take it out, and four faces appear. So the surface goes up by two faces. Here that's two times sixteen, thirty-two.
The middle of a face. It shows only one face. Take it out, or push it in, and five faces appear. So the surface goes up by four faces, sixty-four.
There's a pattern here. The faces we lose plus the faces we gain always make six, the six faces of the cube we removed. And I'll see you in the next question.
